notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check; evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. Model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware run and no hardware backend (the device is a simulated R0 world). Only the 1-vs-1 VolleyBotEnv is served; the 2-vs-2 TeamVolleyBot entry symbol of the card is cited in the facts but not bound by this package. MOCK PATH: the card prefers the upstream simulator, but the hard rules forbid importing or running the clone, so the fake backend is the package's pure-Python reduced model (fake.py). The gate environment has no gym, opencv or Webots Supervisor module (numpy is present, but the clone also needs gym); there is no sim backend because the clone has no gym.envs.registration.register call and an env_id could not be imported safely. The fake was not compared with an upstream run: its physics, baseline opponent, Python random stream and float lists differ from the clone's numpy physics and arrays, and the fidelity gaps disclose all of that. Expected warnings: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (it sets the pending seed only, so it makes no native call) and four G8.NO_UNIT for bridge-derived integer inputs (ticks, action.values[*] and seed twice). G4 has no REF_VALUE or REF_BINARY warnings: every fact cites a text or code line at the pinned commit. Only catalogue classes cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 are used, so there are no catalogue requests and no extension ids. The fake's device-like numbers (start positions, physics constants and canned values) are test data marked as placeholders and are not used as Facts or Limits. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package; gate.digest is the digest line the check printed.
